title: DOTS as a named public-health slogan
dek: Wikipedia's directly observed treatment, short-course is a 1990s programme brand. It is not a 2024 regimen table.
story: DOTS on Wikipedia is the branded WHO strategy of the 1990s: smear microscopy, standardised short-course, directly observed doses, political commitment, recording systems.
Observation of doses still exists as adherence support. The brand is not BPaLM, not Ultra-first diagnosis, not the End TB strategy's full later stack.
This card stops students from treating a historic slogan as current clinical protocol.
deep: Video DOT and community support are modern adherence tools; they are not 'the five elements of DOTS' copied into a 2026 thesis methods section as if nothing changed.
Short-course then meant HRZE-era DS-TB, not HPZM or BPaLM.
Infection-control and WRDs have their own plates.
